document.title: Reagan Letter to Gandhi on Afghanistan
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), A New Phase in the Great Game: U.S., Soviets, India, Pakistan vied to shape a new Afghanistan in late 1980s | National Security Archive
document.note: [Secret] Secret letter before Gandhi's meeting with Gorbachev. Reagan urges Gandhi to press for Soviet withdrawal, says the U.S. does not seek to bleed the Soviets, calls the partial withdrawal phony, and justifies stepped-up security support for Pakistan including early warning capability.

events.description: Gandhi visited Washington and held discussions with Reagan.
Last round of UN-sponsored Afghanistan negotiations produced no forward movement on withdrawal timetable.
Soviet 'phony' partial withdrawal of units, per Reagan.
State Department cable 364282 transmits Reagan's secret letter to Gandhi on Afghanistan and US security assistance to Pakistan.
Rajiv Gandhi visited Washington and held discussions with Reagan.
Gandhi remarked in Harare that he wished an end to intervention and interference in Afghanistan by all parties.
Last round of UN-sponsored Afghanistan talks produced no movement on the Soviet withdrawal timetable.
Soviet 'phony' partial withdrawal of units staged in front of cameras.
Soviet and Kabul regime forces made about 650 incursions into Pakistani airspace and territory, a 154 percent increase over the prior year.
Reagan's secret letter to Gandhi on Afghanistan and security assistance to Pakistan, sent via State Department cable 364282.

relationships.detail: Reagan and Gandhi held discussions in Washington in June 1985.
relationships.quote: WHEN YOU VISITED WASHINGTON IN JUNE 1985, OUR DISCUSSIONS MARKED A NEW STEP FORWARD

relationships.detail: Gandhi has upcoming discussions with the Soviet General Secretary; Reagan urges him to raise Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: YOUR UPCOMING DISCUSSIONS WITH THE GENERAL SECRETARY COULD HELP TO ADVANCE THE PROCESS

relationships.detail: Whitehead signed the State Department cable conveying Reagan's letter.
relationships.quote: KABUL MINIMIZE CONSIDERED. WHITEHEAD

relationships.detail: Soviet and regime forces jointly committed cross-border violations of Pakistan.
relationships.quote: SOVIET AND KABUL REGIME CROSS-BORDER VIOLATIONS OF PAKISTANI AIRSPACE AND TERRITORY HAVE INCREASED

relationships.detail: US resumed arms sales relationship with Pakistan, affected by Soviet military action.
relationships.quote: OUR RESUMED ARMS SALES RELATIONSHIP WITH PAKISTAN

relationships.detail: Reagan writes to Gandhi urging him to raise the Afghan issue and a withdrawal timetable with the Soviet General Secretary.
relationships.quote: I AM WRITING TO YOU NOW ON THE SUBJECTS: AFGHANISTAN AND U.S. SECURITY ASSISTANCE TO PAKISTAN.

relationships.detail: Gandhi had contacts with the Soviets on Afghanistan and was due to hold upcoming discussions with the General Secretary.
relationships.quote: I BELIEVE YOUR UPCOMING DISCUSSIONS WITH THE GENERAL SECRETARY COULD HELP TO ADVANCE THE PROCESS TOWARD A SETTLEMENT

relationships.detail: Gandhi's contacts with the Soviets on Afghanistan after the 1985 Washington visit were welcomed by Reagan.
relationships.quote: YOUR CONTACTS WITH THE SOVIETS ON THE AFGHAN PROBLEM AFTER YOUR VISIT TO WASHINGTON LAST YEAR WERE MOST WELCOME.

relationships.detail: US raised a comprehensive Afghanistan settlement with the Soviets repeatedly in 1986.
relationships.quote: IN REPEATED CONVERSATIONS WITH THE SOVIETS THIS YEAR, WE HAVE MADE CLEAR TO THEM OUR INTEREST IN A COMPREHENSIVE SETTLEMENT

relationships.detail: US resumed an arms sales relationship with Pakistan, affected by Soviet military action in Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: OUR RESUMED ARMS SALES RELATIONSHIP WITH PAKISTAN, AS YOU KNOW, IS DIRECTLY AFFECTED BY ESCALATING SOVIET MILITARY ACTION IN AFGHANISTAN

relationships.detail: Soviet and Kabul regime forces are jointly cited for cross-border violations of Pakistan.
relationships.quote: SOVIET AND KABUL REGIME CROSS-BORDER VIOLATIONS OF PAKISTANI AIRSPACE AND TERRITORY HAVE INCREASED

relationships.detail: Soviet forces occupy Afghanistan; US demands their withdrawal.
relationships.quote: THROUGH THE PROMPT AND COMPLETE WITHDRAWAL OF SOVIET FORCES.

relationships.detail: US opposes Soviet occupation and seeks withdrawal, while denying a goal of bleeding the Soviets.
relationships.quote: WE DO NOT SEEK TO BLEED THE SOVIETS IN AFGHANISTAN BY PROLONGING THE WAR.

relationships.detail: US considering enhanced early warning capability for Pakistan and will keep India's concerns in mind.
relationships.quote: WE WILL KEEP IN MIND YOUR GOVERNMENT'S CONCERNS AS WE MOVE TO A DECISION ON THIS.

relationships.detail: UN-sponsored negotiations are stalemated over the length of the Soviet withdrawal timetable.
relationships.quote: THE UN-SPONSORED NEGOTIATIONS ARE STALEMATED OVER THE LENGTH OF THE SOVIET WITHDRAWAL TIMETABLE.

relationships.detail: Message sent over Whitehead's name from State.
relationships.quote: KABUL MINIMIZE CONSIDERED. WHITEHEAD

relationships.detail: Cable instructs the embassy in New Delhi to convey the letter immediately.
relationships.quote: POST SHOULD IMMEDIATELY CONVEY LETTER IN PARA 3 FROM PRESIDENT REAGAN TO PRIME MINISTER GANDHI.

relationships.detail: Reagan is the US President writing the letter.
relationships.quote: PRESIDENT REAGAN TO PRIME MINISTER GANDHI

relationships.detail: Gandhi is Prime Minister of India.
relationships.quote: PRESIDENT REAGAN TO PRIME MINISTER GANDHI

relationships.detail: Gorbachev is the General Secretary (inferred) of the Soviet Union.
relationships.quote: I URGE YOU TO USE YOUR TALKS WITH THE GENERAL SECRETARY

key_claims: The US told India it does not seek to bleed the Soviets by prolonging the war and favors a comprehensive political settlement.
The US offered to act as guarantor of a settlement restoring Afghan non-alignment, independence and territorial integrity via complete Soviet withdrawal.
Reagan called the Soviet three-to-four-year withdrawal timeframe untenable and the October 1986 partial withdrawal phony.
US arms sales to Pakistan are tied to escalating Soviet and Kabul regime cross-border incursions, said to total 650 in 1986.
The US is considering an enhanced early-warning capability for Pakistan and will keep Indian concerns in mind.
UN-sponsored negotiations were stalemated over the length of the Soviet withdrawal timetable.
